definitions.explanation: A native Japanese counter that can be used for various objects, especially when the specific counter is unknown. Only used for numbers 1-9.

examples.japanese: {一|ひと}つ⟦ください→ください：02899_kudasai⟧。
⟦りんご→りんご：02269_ringo⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{三|みっ}つ⟦ください→ください：02899_kudasai⟧。
⟦{問題|もんだい}→問題：00797_mondai⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{二|ふた}つ⟦あります→ある：00006_aru⟧。

examples.english: There are four windows in the room.

examples.japanese: ⟦お{菓子|かし}→お菓子：02852_okashi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{八|やっ}つ⟦ありました→ある：00006_aru⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧、{五|いつ}つ⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{子供|こども}→子供：00554_kodomo⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦あげました→あげる：00546_ageru⟧。{三|みっ}つ⟦{残|のこ}りました→残る：01187_nokoru⟧。
examples.english: There were eight sweets, but I gave five to the children. Three remained.

notes: つ uses native Japanese numbers (not Chinese-derived): {一|ひと}つ, {二|ふた}つ, {三|みっ}つ, {四|よっ}つ, {五|いつ}つ, {六|むっ}つ, {七|なな}つ, {八|やっ}つ, {九|ここの}つ. For 10 and above, use ⟦{十|とお}→十：00708_juu⟧ (ten) or the Chinese-derived numbers with appropriate counters. This counter is very useful when you don't know the specific counter for something.
